APPROVED ON SEPTEMBER 2, 2026

**REGULAR MEETING OF THE SOUTH BURLINGTON SCHOOL BOARD**

Wednesday, August 19, 2026
Executive Session at 5:00 pm
Regular Session at 6:00 pm
South Burlington School District Administrative Office
577 Dorset Street, South Burlington, VT

## REGULAR MEETING

### PRESENT
Seamus Abshere, Jennifer Lawrence, Dan Boyer, Michelle Boyer, Elissa Galvez, Tom Chittenden

### ADMINISTRATION/STAFF
Dr. Joe Clark, Jean-Marie Clark, Daisy Brayton, Nicole Carter, Nick Bocchino

### GUESTS
Mick Leddy

### Call Regular meeting to order
Seamus Abshere, called the meeting to order at 5:30 p.m.

## EXECUTIVE SESSION
The Board convened in Executive Session at 5:30 p.m.

Seamus Abshere called for a motion to enter executive session at 5:30 p.m. to discuss employment of a public officer or employee, labor negotiations, and receiving confidential attorney-client communication for the purpose of providing legal services to the Board as permitted under Vermont law and added that it would be significantly disadvantageous to the district not to do so in executive session.

Jennifer Lawrence moves, and Dan Boyer seconds. All in favor and the motion passes.

Discuss labor negotiations, employment of a public officer, and receive confidential attorney-client communication for the purpose of providing legal services to the board.

IN: 5:30 p.m.
OUT: 6:05 p.m.
Emilee Hoffman arrived at 5:35 p.m. (phone)
No Action.

Dan Boyer moved to adjourn the executive session at 6:05 p.m. Elissa Galvez seconds. All in favor and the motion passes. The executive session was adjourned at 6:05 p.m.
The board returned to the regular meeting at 6:05 p.m.

## REGULAR MEETING

### Present
Seamus Abshere, Jennifer Lawrence, Dan Boyer, Michelle Boyer, Elissa Galvez, Tom Chittenden, Momin Waqar, Oliver Kunz, Charu Magar

### Administration/Staff
Dr. Joe Clark, Jean-Marie Clark, Daisy Brayton, Nicole Carter, Nick Bocchino, Suzanne Gruendling, Lissa McDonald, Holly Rouelle, Kat Yun

### Guests
Gerry Silverstein (online), Bryan Companion (online)

### Call to Order
Chair Seamus Abshere called the meeting to order at 6:05 p.m. The Pledge of Allegiance was said.

## ANNOUNCEMENTS AND AMENDMENTS TO THE AGENDA

### Announcements
There were no announcements.

### Comments and Questions
No public comments were received.

### Focus on Student Learning
Oliver Kunz explained how students are wrapping up their summer activities as the upcoming academic school year begins on the 24th for incoming 9th graders and the 25th for all other students. The 2026 SLAM leaders at the high school are getting prepared for the incoming freshman class. All the SLAM leaders are going to the Hulbert Outdoor Center tomorrow to engage in team building and leadership activities.

Charu Magar stated that all sports have begun; field hockey, soccer, volleyball, cross-country, and football.

Oliver Kunz said that was the end of the student report.

There were no questions.

Seamus Abshere questioned the 24th being the first day of school, as he believed it was the 25th. Olivier Kunz said yes, school starts on the 25th for 9th graders and the 26th for all students.

## COMMUNITY FORUM ITEMS

### Discuss First Draft of the Ends Policy Update
The board introduced the agenda item as a community forum item for updating the first reading of the District's Ends Policy. Seamus Abshere began by providing viewers with some context, explaining how the Ends Policy is a foundational document of the District's governance policy and is like the Constitution of the District. The policy outlines what is important, how things are done and what things need to happen. He further explained how the policy was written about 12 years ago and that this is the first time it has been updated in those 12 years. The process began in January and since then there has been about 6 community forums, about 8 - 10 times of the board talking about it, and focus groups. There was also a community survey and that is what is being looked at now; the outcome of that survey.

Seamus Abshere explained that he would read aloud the proposed New Ends Policy (first reading), not as a requirement, but because of the importance of the document. He mentioned how the board tries to use as few words as possible and they try to make sure that every word has a reason behind it. He used section 1.1.1 as an example of keeping the document cut and dry and so the board has tried to maintain that standard throughout the whole document.

Dan Boyer stated that Oliver Kunz wrote something last week about adding more history and social studies to the Ends Policy. Michelle Boyer explained that it was also under the skills section of expected outcomes, so the board separated these because they are truly academic areas; to include them in 1.1 and then expand on it in the co-curriculars and then took the list of the remaining standards off of the Vermont Educational Standards site. She stated that one of the benefits of this approach is that it aligns exactly with the EQS, so it does not set two different targets for the District and that ideally it will increase the likelihood that these will be connected and will hopefully decrease some of the frustrations, difficulties and challenges associated with trying to align what is said in the District standards with what's in the Vermont State Standards. Seamus Abshere began to explain why social studies is not listed in section 1.1.1 and then Michelle Boyer said that is a clear emphasis on those four academic subjects and those are the ones for which there are consistent measures. Seamus Abshere asked Michelle Boyer to talk about the word "well-rounded". She described the word as a breakdown between achievement and skills and what the board heard from the community very strongly, was the need to elevate those so-called transferable skills to improve learning and to be prepared to live in the adult world; things like strong communication, personal accountability, showing up on time, finishing assignments on time, arriving to class prepared.

Seamus Abshere asked the board to discuss why readiness for adult life was separated from well-rounded skills. Michelle Boyer explained that this had more to do with what outcome is wanted for students in terms of skills; where preparedness for adult life is more on the being aware of what the opportunities are that are available to students, getting the kinds of support that is needed to pursue, and then actually make plans for pursuing based on a person's skills, interests, passions. She still feels that there is more wordsmithing to do with this draft.

Seamus Abshere stated that one of the goals from the beginning has been to provide the Superintendent something that is measurable, as the original Ends Policy could be hard to pin down, as the board previously agreed. The one bullet point, and something the Superintendent will be tested on, is if the kids are taking age-appropriate steps. That is really what needs to be highlighted. He also would like to highlight and to clearly communicate here that college is not the only path and to put some emphasis that preparation does not start when everyone is applying for college. Superintendent Joe Clark explained that naturally the District would want to follow up on students because they are not done when they leave school. Knowing what they are doing, such as, enrolled in school or working at a job, would be helpful data to evaluate how successful the District was in preparing them. He said that would be the gold standard.

Seamus Abshere discussed the difference between the previous policy and this policy is that it requires the superintendent to ask the community what they think and what is being said is that, similar to the academic rigor part, is that we want things to improve and the line to go up. He said this would be something that he would expect to be monitored.

Kat Yun described her initial thoughts on the proposed Ends Policy and how she originally wanted to cull out the multilingual students and the historically marginalized groups because of how it was phrased. She feels there is a lot of value in identifying the additional groups in terms of being obligated to ensure they are meeting those standards of success. Some word tweaking can make a difference in how a phrase is interpreted.

The board continued through the sections with various discussions surrounding use of words and ownership by students and District.

Seamus Abshere explained this was the first reading and there will be a second reading to continue the discussion. He asked if there were any further questions. Elissa Galvez questioned if there would need to be another first reading if anything changed on the draft from this meeting. Seamus Abshere said no since the changes were not substantial. Michelle Boyer said it gives the opportunity to keep working on it and keep getting feedback to further make updates.

## DISCUSSION ITEMS

### Revised Executive Limitation 2.4 Financial Condition and Activities
Seamus Abshere explained how this was discussed last week in the context of a proposal from the superintendent to change it. That was not considered a first reading, because it was just a proposal from the superintendent, but the board asked him last week to look at the proposed changes and put it up for a first reading. The only thing he recommends changing is to raise the bidding limit on #6 from $25,000 to $40,000 and Joe Clark continued to say the change would reflect the State Law bidding requirement of $40,000. Tom Chittenden questioned if anyone checked with the Vermont School Boards Association (VSBA) for model policy and Joe Clark answered they had not because it would be part of the policy governance and not just the traditional policies. He also mentioned that one of the employees in the business office is the president of her state organization and had shared feedback. Seamus Abshere looked up Tom Chittenden's question and the VSBA has their model policy at $20,000 and then asked Joe Clark, as an action item for the next board meeting, to look at that model policy as suggested by Tom Chittenden. Seamus Abshere stated that he will edit the draft to be $40,000 instead of the $25,000.

### Monthly Financial Report
Jean-Marie Clark presented the FY26 Pre-Audit YTD Financial Report as of 8/14/2026 to the board. She presented the expenses for the fiscal year and discussed the $71 million Working Budget from last year. She explained that the Working Budget is named as such because things are moved around a little over time as the year goes by, as needs change, so it may look a little different than exactly what was proposed at the beginning of the budget year. She continued to describe each column on the report. She highlighted the Pre-Audit Balance is around $1.5 million which is about 2.15% of the budget, which is really good in a $71 million budget.

Jean-Marie Clark then provided an overview of the general fund revenue and explained why a couple of lines are in red. She stated that as of right now, the District is anticipating a surplus of $1.79 million which is the result of underspending the approved expenditure budget, and receiving more offsetting revenues than originally budgeted. She is really happy overall with how the fiscal year ended and said they have talked about what to do with the excess money. She explained three possible choices: 1.) put the money towards the new budget year and buy down the tax rate; 2.) move some [money] into a capital reserve; or 3.) move into an operational savings reserve which is really like an educational stabilization fund, to help non capital and non facility issues.

Jean-Marie Clark continued to discuss the budget lines in the financial report and provided an overview of salaries, unencumbered money, posted and open positions.

## ACTION ITEMS

Seamus Abshere called for a motion to appoint an additional board member to the Act 170 Merger Committee. Based on weighted pupils, South Burlington must appoint 2 board members if Winooski appoints 1, which is the current plan. If Winooski decides to appoint 2, then we must appoint 3. Dan Boyer volunteered. Seamus Abshere entertained a motion to nominate Dan Boyer to be the second board member for the Act 170 Merger Committee.

Tom Chittenden moves, Elissa Galvez seconds. No discussion. All in favor and motion passes.

## SUPERINTENDENT'S REPORT

Dr. Joe Clark provided a brief update on the Chittenden Central Cooperative Educational Service Area (CESA). He was currently elected as Chair for CESA, which includes Burlington, Colchester, Essex/Westford, South Burlington, and Winooski. The CESA board has met twice and is beginning the work of establishing the organization required under Act 170. The CESA board confirmed recently that regular meetings will be held on the fourth Monday of each month from 6:00 p.m. to 7:30 p.m., beginning September 28th, at 577 Dorset Street in South Burlington. He explained that much of the discussion during the last meeting focused on the significant number of implementation questions that remain unanswered. There was strong interest among CESA board members in having the state provide coordinated guidance, model documents, and training so that CESA can begin operating consistently and efficiently. Joe Clark explained how he sent a letter on behalf of the CESA board to the Agency of Education, the Governor's office, Legislative leadership, education committee chairs, and legislators representing the five member communities asking for that support. He mentioned the next meeting is scheduled for September 28th and will keep the South Burlington School Board informed as work develops.

## CONSENT AGENDA
Seamus Abshere presented the Consent Agenda for Board consideration.

Items approved included:

### Hire(s) - One-year only positions
- **Katherine Lafont**, 1.0 FTE Special Educator at Orchard School. Katherine is replacing the resignation of Andrea Ustianov.
- **Rebecca Mellen**, .40 FTE Math Teacher at South Burlington High School. Rebecca is an addition to staff.
- **Megan Ozog**, 1.0 FTE Special Educator at Frederick H. Tuttle Middle School. Megan is an addition to staff.

Seamus Abshere asked if there were any objections to the Consent Agenda. Hearing none. Agenda is passed by consent.

## AGENDA FOR NEXT MEETING

Set agenda for September 2, 2026, regular meeting and review future agenda items/ parking lot. Add the following items to the September 2 agenda: 1.) Ends Policy update (second reading) set as a community forum; 2.) Revised Executive Limitation 2.4 Financial Condition and Activities (second reading).

Joe Clark believes the Monitoring Report 2.3 Treatment of Community is now an external review which means someone outside of the district would need to review it. Seamus Abshere will look into that and will assign himself the task.

Seamus Abshere asked if board members would like anything added under the Superintendent's Report for the next meeting. Jennifer Lawrence asked for website updates and Joe Clark said to add the start of the school year.

Joe Clark reminded the board that starting in September, the second meeting of each month, the principals will attend with students to do a short presentation on something cool that is going on in their building.

## ADJOURNMENT

There being no further business, Seamus Abshere called for a motion to adjourn. Elissa Galvez moved and Dan Boyer seconded. Motion carried unanimously and the meeting adjourned at 8:22 p.m.
